## 1. Status at a glance
- Issue #30, "Peer-range bump to admit bareguard 0.13.x (conditional — only if bareguard 0.13.0 ships)".
- State: **Closed / completed** (hamr0, Aug 13). Label: `dependencies` only. No assignee, no milestone, no projects, no relationships, **no priority set**.
- Resolution: shipped in **v0.36.1** (published to npm, `latest`), PR **#31**, tag **v0.36.1**.

## 2. What was at stake (for context, already resolved)
- bare-agent 0.36.0 pinned the optional peer `bareguard` to `>=0.9.0 <0.13.0`. That `<0.13.0` ceiling would make bare-agent 0.36.0 **refuse to install** alongside bareguard 0.13.x — an install-time peer-range conflict, even though the adapter was already compliant.
- bareguard 0.13.0 hardened the `gate.annotate` array fail-open: `surface` must be an explicit boolean, else the row is malformed → buffer nothing, never throw, emit a distinct `annotate_malformed` audit row. That is a gate-behaviour + audit-format change, cut as a minor pre-1.0.
- **No code fault on the bare-agent side.** `judgeToAnnotation` (src/bareguard-adapter.js) returns a single object literal and always sets `surface: v.verdict !== 'honored'` — an explicit boolean — so it satisfied the new rule by construction. The fix was a manifest range bump only.

## 3. What was actually done (verify, don't redo)
1. bareguard 0.13.0 went live.
2. Peer **and** dev ranges widened to `>=0.9.0 <0.14.0` (conservative `<0.14.0` ceiling).
3. No code change — `judgeToAnnotation` confirmed already compliant (single object literal, explicit-boolean `surface`, `String()`-coerced JSON-safe `meta`).
4. Validated against bareguard 0.13.0: bareguard-touching tests **84/84**, CI full suite green.

## 4. Recommended first response (≈10 minutes)
1. **Confirm you're on the fixed line:** check the installed/published bare-agent is **0.36.1 or later** (`latest` on npm). If a reporter is on 0.36.0, the guidance is simply "upgrade to 0.36.1".
2. **Sanity-check the manifest**, not the source: `package.json` peer + dev ranges should both read `>=0.9.0 <0.14.0`. If they do, #30 is fully satisfied.
3. **Reply to any inbound report** pointing at v0.36.1 / PR #31 and close it as a duplicate of #30's fix. No new issue needed.
4. **Do not re-run the audit/gate work.** The malformed-fact rule is satisfied by construction; there is no bare-agent-side `annotate_malformed` handling to add.

## 5. Fastest rollback / escalation
- If bareguard 0.13.x turns out to misbehave in the field, the reversible lever is the manifest only: re-narrow the peer range to `<0.13.0` and cut a patch. Because the adapter code was never touched, **there is no code to revert** — no risk of regressing `judgeToAnnotation`.
- Escalate to hamr0 (issue author, repo owner, only participant; cross-repo coordination with the bareguard maintainer happened 2026-08-12) if a bareguard 0.14 pre-release appears — the `<0.14.0` ceiling was chosen conservatively and will need the same review before it blocks installs.

- Metadata shows "No branches or pull requests" under Development, yet the activity references PR #31 and tag v0.36.1. Reads as a cross-repo/PR-not-linked-in-Development artifact, not a missing fix. If you need the diff, look up PR #31 directly before assuming anything beyond the manifest bump.
